title: Run both starter applications
firstStep: Start the frontend and API; visit / and /health.
lesson: A browser page and an API response are different HTTP representations.
assessment: Which app returns HTML, which returns JSON, and why is there one lockfile?
acceptance: A fresh npm ci succeeds.
Both apps run and you record their addresses and one Network-panel observation.

title: Inventory the Figma reference
firstStep: List the visible sections, screens and interactive states in your Figma Make file.
lesson: A design inventory turns a visual reference into explicit implementation scope.
assessment: Which parts are presentation, interaction, or data-backed features?
acceptance: Record actual sections, assets, routes, desktop/mobile behavior and states.
Flag uncertain features instead of assuming the scaffold includes them.

title: Define portfolio content and API contracts
firstStep: Write sample project data and decide what needs persistence.
lesson: A contract defines request, response and error shapes before either side depends on them.
assessment: Which content can stay static, and what justifies a database or admin login?
acceptance: Document public content, editable content, contact requirements and non-goals.
Define draft endpoint shapes and decide whether admin auth is required.

title: Practice branches, commits and pull requests
firstStep: Create a branch and submit a small README improvement.
lesson: A small PR preserves one clear reason for a change.
assessment: How do a branch, commit, issue and pull request relate?
acceptance: Link the issue in a focused PR.
Run checks and explain the change without submitting unrelated files.

title: Choose and load portfolio fonts
firstStep: Identify font families in the reference and check their licenses.
lesson: Typography needs readable sizes, fallbacks and predictable loading.
assessment: What happens when a font fails to load, and what causes layout shift?
acceptance: Document font sources, permitted use and fallbacks.
Use Next.js font loading or local fonts; verify readable text and no avoidable layout shift.

title: Define colors, spacing and type tokens
firstStep: List repeated colors, spacing and text sizes from the reference.
lesson: Tokens give repeated design choices one consistent name.
assessment: When is a token useful compared with a one-off style?
acceptance: Create documented CSS/Tailwind tokens for color, type, spacing, radius and focus.
Check text/background contrast and use tokens in one small sample.

title: Build light and dark theme behavior
firstStep: Describe initial theme, system preference and manual toggle behavior.
lesson: Theme state affects rendering, persistence and accessible contrast.
assessment: How can a saved browser preference cause a hydration mismatch?
acceptance: Implement and persist an accessible theme switch with a system fallback.
Verify contrast, keyboard operation, initial load and no hydration warnings.

title: Set global custom styles and responsive rules
firstStep: Write base heading, paragraph, link and focus styles.
lesson: Responsive design adapts content rather than assuming one device size.
assessment: Why can a fixed-width container fail on a small screen?
acceptance: Define consistent base styles and responsive content widths.
Check narrow mobile, tablet and desktop widths with no horizontal overflow.

title: Create the shared Button component
firstStep: Specify primary, secondary, disabled and focus states.
lesson: A reusable button should preserve native semantics and expose only necessary options.
assessment: When should navigation use a link instead of a button?
acceptance: Build Button with accessible states and minimal props.
Add the first real exports/React peer dependencies to packages/ui and demonstrate consumption.

title: Create inputs and form feedback
firstStep: Build one labeled input with hint and error text.
lesson: Labels and error associations make forms usable beyond visual layout.
assessment: Why is a placeholder not a label?
acceptance: Support label, hint, error, disabled and required states.
Verify keyboard use and programmatically associated error text.

title: Create ProgressBar and indicator states
firstStep: Decide whether the reference represents measurable progress or decoration.
lesson: A progress indicator needs a meaningful accessible value or an explicit indeterminate state.
assessment: What should assistive technology announce when progress is unknown?
acceptance: Create ProgressBar only for a meaningful use found in the reference.
Verify bounds/accessible values or document why a decorative indicator replaces it.

title: Build the responsive page shell
firstStep: Create semantic header, navigation, main and footer regions.
lesson: Landmarks and skip links make the page easier to navigate.
assessment: Which landmark should contain the primary page content?
acceptance: Implement desktop/mobile navigation and a skip link.
Verify keyboard focus, mobile menu behavior and no content obstruction.

title: Build the introduction and about sections
firstStep: Write your real introductory text and section hierarchy.
lesson: Semantic structure conveys meaning before styling is applied.
assessment: How do heading levels help someone scan a page without seeing its layout?
acceptance: Implement only sections confirmed by the inventory with real approved content.
Check headings, readable text, mobile layout and links.

title: Build skills and journey sections
firstStep: Map the reference's skills or timeline content into data.
lesson: Repeated UI should be driven by stable data and meaningful keys.
assessment: Why can array-index keys be unstable when a list changes?
acceptance: Build the confirmed skills/journey content without invented claims.
Verify ordered reading, narrow layouts and meaningful indicators.

title: Build project cards and project details
firstStep: Create one sample project card and its detail route.
lesson: Routes identify content; components share presentation.
assessment: What should happen when a project slug is unknown?
acceptance: Render projects from a clear data shape with stable routes and accessible links.
Add a useful not-found state and responsive images/details.

title: Build the contact form interface
firstStep: Define fields and submit/success/failure states before wiring an API.
lesson: Client validation improves feedback but cannot protect the server.
assessment: Which validations must also run on the backend?
acceptance: Use labeled inputs, validation feedback and pending/success/error states.
Prevent accidental duplicate submits and preserve input after recoverable failures.

title: Polish motion and reduced-motion behavior
firstStep: Inventory the reference's interactions and choose one small animation.
lesson: Motion should explain state without blocking access to content.
assessment: How would you respect a user's reduced-motion setting?
acceptance: Implement only purposeful transitions confirmed by the reference.
Verify reduced-motion preferences, focus and performance on mobile.

title: Validate environment configuration and database startup
firstStep: List required settings and separate local defaults from production requirements.
lesson: Failing clearly at startup is safer than discovering missing settings during a request.
assessment: When should /health differ from a database-readiness check?
acceptance: Create validated config with useful errors and no secret values in logs.
Connect Mongoose with explicit startup/failure/shutdown behavior and update env examples.

title: Design project schemas and indexes
firstStep: Write the smallest persisted project schema from the API contract.
lesson: Schemas validate structure; indexes support queries and constraints.
assessment: Why does application validation alone not guarantee uniqueness?
acceptance: Define project fields, allowed values, timestamps and needed indexes.
Verify invalid data and duplicate constraints against a test database.

title: Implement validation and safe API errors
firstStep: Define success and invalid-input responses for one endpoint.
lesson: Controllers map HTTP, services handle use cases, and validators constrain input.
assessment: Why should the API avoid returning raw database errors?
acceptance: Add strict request validation, identifier checks and centralized safe errors.
Prove malformed JSON, invalid fields, unknown routes and unexpected errors return safe responses.

title: Implement public project read endpoints
firstStep: Implement the contracted project-list response first.
lesson: Public reads still need bounded queries and safe response shapes.
assessment: What happens if a caller requests an extremely large page size?
acceptance: Provide bounded list and slug/detail reads with only public fields.
Test success, missing records, invalid query values and stable response contracts.

title: Implement the contact-submission endpoint
firstStep: Validate one synthetic contact submission without sending real email.
lesson: Untrusted input must be constrained before persistence or delivery.
assessment: How could an otherwise valid contact endpoint be abused?
acceptance: Implement strict field/size validation and the agreed storage/delivery policy.
Verify invalid input, safe responses, duplicate/abuse handling and no private message text in logs.

title: Apply HTTP security and CORS policy
firstStep: List the exact frontend origins allowed in local and deployed environments.
lesson: CORS controls browser reads; it is not authentication or authorization.
assessment: Can a command-line client call an API even when CORS denies its origin?
acceptance: Configure Helmet, explicit CORS origins, body limits and baseline rate limiting.
Test allowed/disallowed origins, large bodies and rate-limit behavior; document proxy assumptions.

title: Decide the admin authentication and authorization model
firstStep: Decide whether portfolio updates actually need an admin UI.
lesson: Authentication identifies someone; authorization decides permitted actions.
assessment: Why should a public portfolio not require public account registration by default?
acceptance: Record admin scope, account provisioning, credential/session transport and ownership policy.
If no admin auth is needed, document N/A and close conditional auth tasks deliberately.

title: Implement conditional admin login with bcrypt and JWT
firstStep: If auth is required, first test wrong-password behavior with synthetic accounts.
lesson: bcrypt hashes passwords; JWT signatures protect claims but do not hide them.
assessment: What belongs in a JWT, and what checks are needed beyond decoding it?
acceptance: If required, use bcrypt, minimal safe claims, expiry and explicit JWT algorithm/issuer/audience policy.
Test valid/wrong credentials, expired/tampered tokens and protected-resource authorization.

title: Implement conditional session invalidation and account recovery
firstStep: Write reset/change/logout behavior before choosing token storage.
lesson: A password reset is incomplete if unwanted sessions remain usable.
assessment: How do expiry, revocation and a one-use recovery token differ?
acceptance: If required, define revocation and secure reset/change behavior; add email verification only if needed.
Verify expiry, single use, token hashing, enumeration protection and account/IP abuse limits.

title: Protect conditional project content mutations
firstStep: Start with a test showing an unauthorized edit is rejected.
lesson: Every write needs a field allow-list and permission decision.
assessment: Why is passing request.body directly to a database update risky?
acceptance: If admin editing is required, implement validated authorized create/update/delete operations.
Test missing credentials, insufficient permissions, invalid identifiers and forbidden fields.

title: Add redacted logging and graceful shutdown
firstStep: List useful operational events and sensitive fields that must be excluded.
lesson: Logs should explain failures without becoming a second store of secrets.
assessment: What must never be logged from an authentication or contact request?
acceptance: Use structured redacted logs and safe security events where applicable.
Demonstrate clean shutdown of HTTP/database resources and safe unexpected-error handling.

title: Connect project UI to the Express API
firstStep: Fetch the project-list contract and show a loading state.
lesson: Network requests can fail independently of the page rendering.
assessment: How will the UI distinguish an empty result from a failed request?
acceptance: Configure a single API base URL and connect project list/detail views.
Verify loading, empty, error, success and unknown-project behavior without leaking server secrets.

title: Connect the contact form end to end
firstStep: Submit one synthetic message locally and inspect the HTTP response.
lesson: A good integration maps server validation errors into actionable UI feedback.
assessment: Why should a failed request not erase a person's message?
acceptance: Connect the form to the agreed endpoint and map validation/rate-limit/network failures.
Prove success, failure, repeated clicks and preserved input with synthetic data.

title: Build conditional admin editing UI
firstStep: Only if required, sketch the smallest authorized editing flow.
lesson: Client route guards improve navigation but do not secure API writes.
assessment: Can hiding an Edit button prevent an unauthorized API call?
acceptance: If required, connect authenticated content editing to protected backend routes.
Verify unauthorized access, session expiry, validation and server-enforced permissions.

title: Audit accessibility and responsive behavior
firstStep: Navigate the site using only a keyboard at a narrow viewport.
lesson: Automated tools catch some accessibility issues; real interaction checks remain essential.
assessment: What makes a visible focus indicator usable on both themes?
acceptance: Check landmarks, headings, forms, contrast, image text, focus and reduced motion.
Record and fix issues found at mobile/tablet/desktop widths and with a screen-reader spot check.

title: Add meaningful frontend and API regression tests
firstStep: Choose one user-visible failure mode and write a failing test.
lesson: Tests are most valuable when they prove an observable contract or interaction.
assessment: What bug would your test catch that a snapshot alone would miss?
acceptance: Add UI interaction tests and API happy/negative-path integration tests using isolated synthetic data.
Cover auth/security cases only where implemented and keep CI deterministic.

title: Improve SEO, metadata and asset performance
firstStep: Measure one page before optimizing its largest image.
lesson: Performance work should use measurements; metadata helps previews and discovery.
assessment: What is the difference between a social preview image and an image alt description?
acceptance: Add real metadata, social previews, favicon, robots and sitemap appropriate to launch.
Optimize images/fonts, check layout shift and record before/after performance evidence.

title: Review dependency health and CI coverage
firstStep: Run the complete workspace checks and inspect their actual coverage.
lesson: A green build does not prove every user flow is correct.
assessment: What does the starter backend lint command check, and what does it omit?
acceptance: Confirm install/lint/tests/build work from a clean checkout and expand lint/test coverage as code grows.
Review dependency advisories, ignored secrets and CI results; fix material findings.

title: Choose frontend/API/database hosting and document costs
firstStep: Compare one suitable host per app and record the smallest needed resources.
lesson: Hosting choices affect runtime, networking, secrets and ongoing costs.
assessment: Which data must survive a process restart, and where should it live?
acceptance: Choose frontend, Node API and MongoDB hosting based on actual requirements and an approved budget.
Document domains, regions, CORS origins, environment variables and rollback approach before spending.

title: Provision production database and secrets safely
firstStep: List production secrets without putting values in Git.
lesson: Production credentials belong in host secret settings, not frontend bundles.
assessment: How would you rotate a leaked database credential without editing source code?
acceptance: Configure least-privilege database access, network policy and backup/restore expectations.
Validate required settings without printing values; keep development/test data separate.

title: Deploy and verify the API
firstStep: Deploy a reviewed commit and inspect startup and health behavior.
lesson: A process can be alive while a required dependency is unavailable.
assessment: What signal tells you the API is ready to receive real requests?
acceptance: Deploy the API with safe production config, HTTPS, proxy/rate-limit settings and readiness checks.
Verify database access, allowed origins, failures and logs with synthetic requests.

title: Deploy the frontend and configure its domain
firstStep: Build with the production public API URL and verify one API request.
lesson: Public configuration is embedded or served to visitors; secrets must stay server-side.
assessment: Why might changing an environment variable require a rebuild?
acceptance: Deploy the frontend with correct API configuration and HTTPS/domain settings.
Check navigation, assets, forms, metadata, mobile views and both themes against the live API.

title: Run launch review and document maintenance
firstStep: Walk through the deployed site as a first-time visitor.
lesson: Launching includes repeatable operations, monitoring and recovery.
assessment: How would you confirm a rollback restored both the UI and API contracts?
acceptance: Record final accessibility/security/performance checks, functional smoke tests and rollback verification.
Document maintenance, dependency updates, monitoring, backups and known limitations; request final review.
